review_candidates.description: About Us The Center for Regional Economic Competitiveness (CREC) is a 501(c)(3) research nonprofit founded in 2000. We help U.S. regions compete by putting data about regional economies and labor markets to work in economic and workforce development decisions. Our current portfolio includes a multi-year cooperative agreement with the Department of Defense Manufacturing Technology (ManTech) Program and analytical support to the Industrial Base Analysis and Sustainment (IBAS) Program: data-heavy studies of the defense manufacturing base and its supply chains. CREC also manages membership associations of economic and workforce researchers and data users, including the Council for Community and Economic Research (C2ER), the LMI Institute, the State Economic Development Executives, the University Economic Development Association, the Development District Association of Appalachia, and the Projections Managing Partnership, along with partners with Federal, State, and local clients nationwide.  Position Summary & Essential Functions The Senior Program Analyst conducts and coordinates applied research and technical assistance projects, with a concentration in manufacturing, supply chains, and the defense industrial base. The Analyst takes responsibility for defined research components, selects and applies appropriate analytical methods, interprets findings, and produces client-ready reports, presentations, and data products. Working with senior project leaders, the Analyst coordinates assigned work, contributes directly to client discussions, and helps ensure that project deliverables meet CREC’s standards for quality, timeliness, and relevance. The Analyst works across CREC’s portfolio, including multi-year Federal defense industrial base projects, and sees that work published. No security clearance is required. Because the position supports Department of Defense projects that may involve export-controlled information, the Analyst must be a U.S. person (a U.S. citizen or lawful permanent resident).  Essential functions: Design and conduct defined components of applied research and technical assistance projects. Select data sources, research methods, and analytical tools in consultation with project leaders. Collect, clean, integrate, and analyze regional economic, labor market, industry, firm, and supply chain data, including Federal statistical sources such as the Bureau of Labor Statistics, the Census Bureau, and the Bureau of Economic Analysis. Apply quantitative and qualitative methods to supplier identification, industry mapping, demand and supply analysis, and assessments of manufacturing capacity and workforce needs. Use tools such as Excel, R, Python, SQL, GIS, Tableau, or Power BI to produce reproducible analyses and client-ready charts, tables, and maps. Interpret findings, identify implications, and develop evidence-based conclusions and recommendations. Draft substantial sections of research reports, technical memoranda, presentations, and technical assistance materials, and coordinate the preparation of deliverables across multiple contributors. Plan and conduct interviews, focus groups, and other primary research. Present findings and contribute to project team and client discussions. Coordinate defined project components, including schedules, work assignments, quality control, and communication with partners. Review the work of research assistants, interns, or other project contributors when assigned. Contribute to project work plans, scopes of work, budgets, and proposals. Develop deeper expertise in manufacturing, supply chains, defense-related programs, and relevant Federal data systems. As a secondary responsibility, support project logistics, including scheduling, meeting notes, and coordination with partners and clients. The Analyst works with general direction from project leaders and exercises judgment in selecting data sources, applying analytical methods, organizing assigned work, and preparing client-ready products. Senior staff provide guidance on complex methodological, client, and project management issues. Qualifications (Minimum requirements, Preferred credentials) Minimum requirements: Bachelor’s degree in economics, business, engineering, data science, public policy, logistics, supply chain management, or a related field and at least three years of relevant professional experience; or a relevant master’s degree and up to one year of relevant experience. Demonstrated experience conducting applied economic, industry, workforce, manufacturing, or supply chain research. Proficiency in Excel and at least one analytical tool such as R, Python, SQL, GIS, Tableau, or Power BI. Experience selecting and applying quantitative or qualitative research methods. Ability to interpret findings and communicate their implications in clear writing, presentations, tables, and visualizations. Ability to manage multiple assignments, coordinate work with colleagues, and meet project deadlines. Ability to communicate effectively with clients, partners, and other outside contacts. U.S. person status (U.S. citizen or lawful permanent resident). Preferred credentials: Experience in or exposure to defense manufacturing, defense acquisition, or military logistics. Master’s degree in a related field. Experience with Federal statistical data systems, GIS, or data visualization tools. Compensation and Location The salary range for this position is $70,000 to $85,000, depending on experience and education. The position is based in Arlington, Virginia. Infra Solutions is a small, multi-disciplinary team: engineers who are as comfortable operating a system as building one, and as comfortable in a hard conversation as in a code review. review_candidates.description: Job Description Summary Organization's Summary Statement: The Applied Research Laboratory for Intelligence & Security (ARLIS) at the University of Maryland is a University-Affiliated Research Center (UARC) dedicated to advancing research, innovation, and technology transition to improve decision making for U.S. national security. ARLIS combines deep scientific expertise with operational insight to address challenges in intelligence analysis, cybersecurity, artificial intelligence / machine learning, quantum science, and human-machine teaming. Researchers, scientists, engineers, and analysts at ARLIS collaborate with government agencies, industry partners, and academic institutions to deliver actionable insights and transformative solutions through research and development. Employees at ARLIS work on projects of critical importance, contribute directly to the nation's security, and are supported by a culture that values integrity, collaboration, and professional growth. The Quantitative Methods Research Scientist will support ARLIS's expanding research portfolio in operational innovation and information. The role will contribute to a portfolio of government-sponsored projects addressing emerging challenges in areas such as artificial intelligence/machine learning (AI/ML), decision support, information warfare, language assessment and training, natural language processing (NLP), and open-source intelligence (OSINT). The role may include a focus on research development, prototyping, experimentation, systems integration, and/or field deployment. Final appointment title and responsibilities will be based on qualifications and matched to programmatic needs. Must be able to obtain a US security clearance. If selected, must meet the requirements for access to classified information and will be subject to a government security clearance investigation that includes criminal and credit history checks, as well as verification of U.S. citizenship, birth, education, employment, and military history. Final offer is contingent upon the candidate's ability to successfully obtain the necessary interim Secret security clearance, as determined by the government sponsor, prior to commencing employment. Education: Minimum Qualifications: Doctoral degree or Master's and 5 years of research experience in a relevant field, from an accredited college or university. Experience: Evidence of sound scholarly production (e.g., conference presentations, published journal articles, published code, published datasets, technical reports). Demonstrate all the relevant skills required for carrying out quantitative social science research. Background in and demonstrated proficiency with quantitative social science research methods and statistical analyses. Experience leading basic and/or applied research projects. Knowledge, Skills, And Abilities: Extensive experience with one or more statistical analysis programs (e.g., Matlab, R). Skill in research design. Familiarity with social science concepts. Skill in the use of Microsoft Office products. Ability to multi-task and prioritize assignments. Ability to analyze situations and determine the best recourse for response. Physical Demands: Sedentary work performed in a normal office environment; exerts up to 10 pounds of force occasionally and/or negligible amount of force frequently or constantly to lift, carry, push, pull or otherwise move objects, including the human body. Ability to attend meetings both on and off campus. Spending long hours in front of a computer screen. Licenses/Certifications: N/A Education: Preferred Qualifications: Doctoral degree or Master's with 5 years experience in psychology, neuroscience, political science, linguistics, data analytics, computer science, or related field. Experience: Comfort working both independently and collaboratively in a fast-paced, evolving environment. Strong organizational skills and attention to detail. Active, or eligible for a security clearance; prior clearance at SECRET or higher that is active or inactive is preferred; current TS/SCI clearance strongly preferred. Foreign language capabilities, at the advanced level. Programming skills (e.g., Python, C++). Experience working with multidisciplinary project teams. Experience working on federal contracts or grants. Experience with Artificial Intelligence/Machine Learning research. Experience with population modeling. Experience with human subjects research design. Additional Job Details Required Application Materials: Cover Letter, Resume, List of References Best Consideration Date: 10/10/26 Posting Close Date: N/A Open Until Filled: Yes Financial Disclosure Required No For more information on Financial Disclosure, please visit Maryland's State Ethics Commission website. Department VPR-Applied Research Lab for Intelligence & Security Worker Sub-Type Faculty Regular Salary Range $120,000 - $180,000 Benefits Summary For more information on Regular Faculty benefits, select this link. Background Checks Offers of employment are contingent on completion of a background check. Information reported by the background check will not automatically disqualify anyone from employment. Before any adverse decision, the finalist will have an opportunity to provide information to the University regarding disclosable background check information. The University reserves the right to rescind the offer of employment or otherwise decline or terminate employment if the information reported by the background check is deemed incompatible with the position, regardless of when the background check is completed. Employment Eligibility The successful candidate must complete employment eligibility verification (on Form I-9) by presenting documents that establish identity and work authorization within the timeframe required by federal immigration law, and where applicable, to demonstrate renewed employment authorization. Failure to complete employment eligibility verification or reverification within the timeframe set forth by law may result in suspension or termination of employment. EEO Statement The University of Maryland, College Park is an Equal Opportunity Employer. All qualified applicants will receive equal consideration for employment. Please read the University's Equal Employment Opportunity Statement of Policy.
